paths.description: Homepage, primary discovery surface, consent state, performance/security/global template.
Economia section listing, representative section/index template.
Current Cronache story, representative article/detail reading template and metadata.
Newsletter route, representative form/account-adjacent conversion surface.
Invalid route used to evaluate network/HTTP recovery behavior.

findings.summary: A full-viewport consent wall blocks all news on every fresh visit.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360px screenshots show the entire first viewport obscured by a mandatory consent/subscription wall before any article can be read.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking wall with a compact, non-modal consent notice; keep reject and manage choices available without obscuring editorial content.

findings.summary: Consent choices are visually asymmetric and rejection is coupled to subscription.
findings.evidence: The modal gives a dominant filled “ACCETTA E CONTINUA” action while the alternative is “Rifiuta e abbonati”; the free rejection path is not presented as an equal first-level choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer Accept, Reject, and Preferences at the same hierarchy and explain any paid ad-free product separately from privacy consent.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is pixel-equivalent in appearance to the light capture, and computed styles report color-scheme: normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and define preference-driven surface, text, border, and control colors.

findings.summary: Non-essential animations continue under reduced-motion.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found no prefers-reduced-motion CSS rules and five running 2s animations plus running 1.5s animations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce layer that disables non-essential looping and transition animation while preserving state cues.

findings.summary: Navigation changes do not use authored View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found only the browser default view-transition name and no authored transition elements across an MPA with many route changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for same-origin section and article navigation, with reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: The mobile page is a scaled desktop-width layout rather than a true 360px reflow.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport the layout primitive measured innerWidth 1230, visualViewport 1200, clientWidth 1214, and 30px overflow; screenshots show a tiny scaled consent panel.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width and fluid intrinsic layouts; remove fixed 780/1214px page widths and verify true 320–412px reflow.

findings.summary: Components rely on global fixed widths and expose no container-query adaptation.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero CSSContainerRule entries; mobile DOM captures retain 780px main widths and the newsletter form is positioned at x=-352.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type on reusable card/form regions and size-aware @container rules; remove negative off-screen positioning.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is absent on prominent controls.
findings.evidence: The focus probe reported outline-style none and no box-shadow for the first search input and multiple header buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator to every interactive control and test the complete header/menu tab order.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance misses the Core Web Vitals loading bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 12.4s, TBT 560ms and performance 45; the raw-CDP trace measured LCP 3.21s and TBT 311ms, both indicating meaningful delay under their respective conditions.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the actual LCP asset, reduce early script execution, and defer advertising/analytics until after critical editorial content.

findings.summary: Heavy script and layout work blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: Trace found 8 long tasks and 311ms TBT; Lighthouse found 11.2s main-thread work, including 3.0s script evaluation and 2.5s style/layout.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the orchestrator and ad/analytics startup, split long tasks, and schedule non-critical work after interaction-ready content.

findings.summary: The homepage ships a very large and dependency-heavy cold load.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 254 requests and 6.80MB transferred; Lighthouse reported 6.69MiB, 1.2s render-blocking savings and 2.0MiB cache-lifetime savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route budget, shorten critical chains, improve immutable caching, and defer non-critical third-party and below-fold resources.

findings.summary: Large amounts of unused and legacy JavaScript/CSS ship on initial load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 891KiB unused JS, 68KiB unused CSS, 53KiB legacy JS and duplicate module code; HAR records 96 script requests totaling 2.38MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused vendor features, conditionally load ad/analytics/newsletter chunks, modernise bundles, and deduplicate shared modules.

findings.summary: Important controls, links, dialogs, and frames lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 79 and identified unnamed menu/search buttons, unnamed links, an unnamed consent dialog and untitled iframes.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every icon control and linked image a discernible name, repair the dialog label reference, and title meaningful iframes.

findings.summary: Viewport declarations can prevent user zoom and the layout does not reflow cleanly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found duplicate viewport declarations containing maximum-scale=1/user-scalable=no; independent mobile layout evidence shows a 1214px content viewport under 360px emulation.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep one width=device-width, initial-scale=1 viewport declaration without zoom restrictions and implement true narrow-screen reflow.

findings.summary: The homepage logs uncaught and application errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured missing $/jQuery errors, newsletter null.split failures, and an uncaught classList exception.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix dependency ordering and null guards, then make console-error-free loading a release gate.

findings.summary: Image markup and delivery are structurally inefficient.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 16 images without dimensions, 79 without srcset, 94 legacy-format images and 6 missing alt values; Lighthouse also flagged unsized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height, meaningful alt or empty decorative alt, responsive srcset/sizes, and modern AVIF/WebP sources.

findings.summary: Chrome reports browser-platform and cookie inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse best-practices scored 73 and the inspector-issues audit failed with extensive cookie issues; legacy JavaScript was also detected.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve DevTools Issues, modernise legacy bundles, and enforce browser-hygiene checks in CI.

findings.summary: Core browser security headers are absent and cookies are broadly insecure.
findings.evidence: Headers found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, or clickjacking header; cookie audit found 42 cookies flagged insecure, many SameSite=None and several long-lived identifiers.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, and secure cookie defaults; audit each cookie for Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite and lifetime.

findings.summary: The initial page has an exceptionally broad third-party and tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 53 third-party origins and known DoubleClick, Rubicon and GTM trackers; HAR attributes 247/254 requests and 6.53MB to origins classified as third-party.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory vendors, remove low-value trackers, gate optional vendors behind consent, batch analytics, and proxy truly first-party static origins where appropriate.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policies are incomplete.
findings.evidence: No HSTS, CSP/frame-ancestors, X-Frame-Options or X-Content-Type-Options was present; Referrer-Policy remains no-referrer-when-downgrade.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt strict-origin-when-cross-origin, a restrictive Permissions-Policy, CSP frame-ancestors/Trusted Types where feasible, HSTS and nosniff.

findings.summary: Search and text inputs do not expose labels or autocomplete intent.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found visible text inputs with empty autocomplete values and no associated label or aria-label.
findings.suggestedFix: Add programmatic labels, stable name/type/inputmode values, and correct autocomplete tokens for each user-data field.

findings.summary: Image assets consume avoidable bandwidth.
findings.evidence: Images account for 3.77MB; 94/100 use legacy formats, 79 lack srcset, and Lighthouse estimates 1.79MiB image-delivery savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, responsive srcsets and correctly compressed editorial/decorative crops at the rendered size.

findings.summary: Startup performs substantial non-critical advertising and analytics work.
findings.evidence: HAR records 247 third-party requests while Lighthouse reports 891KiB unused JS and 11.2s main-thread work, much of it from tracking/ad vendors.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not start optional vendors before consent or content readiness; lazy-load, batch, and cancel background work when hidden.

findings.summary: Third-party code and media exceed a proportionate news-homepage budget.
findings.evidence: The page transfers 6.80MB over 254 requests, including 2.38MB scripts and 3.77MB images, with 53 third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Set per-template byte/request/third-party budgets and reject additions that exceed them without measured reader value.

findings.summary: The homepage has a disproportionately large in-memory object graph.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary contained 826,807 nodes, 3.17M edges and 58.99MB self size for a document-centric page.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile dominant native/code allocations, unload below-fold widgets and vendor state, and set a steady-state heap/DOM budget.

findings.summary: Rendered article times omit machine-readable, unambiguous datetime values.
findings.evidence: The article probe found many <time> elements with Italian display text but empty dateTime values, while social metadata uses UTC timestamps.
findings.suggestedFix: Populate each time datetime with an ISO 8601 offset/UTC timestamp and render locale/time-zone presentation from that value.

findings.summary: The blocking consent experience is an ad-hoc div dialog rather than a native dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: DOM evidence shows zero <dialog> and popover elements while Lighthouse identifies a full-screen div with role=dialog and a broken accessible name.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native <dialog> only when modality is truly necessary, wire its accessible name, and provide platform dismissal behavior.

findings.summary: Consent chrome occupies 100% of the initial viewport and displaces editorial content.
findings.evidence: Both desktop and mobile screenshots show no readable news content in the unobscured foreground on first load.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the first viewport content-led and move consent controls to a compact, non-obscuring surface.

findings.summary: The visible account entry point provides no evidence of phishing-resistant authentication support.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM/platform probes found no navigator.credentials/WebAuthn-facing affordance or passkey messaging around the account entry point.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and authentication alongside recovery-safe fallbacks, and request credentials only after user action.

findings.summary: The consent/subscription flow conflates privacy rejection with a commercial commitment.
findings.evidence: The only first-level refusal wording is “Rifiuta e abbonati”, while acceptance is free and visually dominant.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate privacy choices from subscription marketing, show commitments and pricing before action, and provide an equal free reject choice.

taskList.title: Decouple privacy consent from subscription and remove the blocking wall
Restore real mobile reflow, zoom, container adaptation and focus
Reduce critical-path JavaScript, third parties and payload weight
Deploy security headers and secure cookie defaults
Fix accessible names, labels and input assistance
Add dark and reduced-motion preference support
Eliminate console/platform errors and reduce heap footprint
